question: A board announces its acquisition will be double-digit accretive to EPS from year one. Does that settle whether shareholders should be pleased?
model_answer_md:
No. Accretion and value creation are different calculations that happen to share a press release.

Accretion asks whether pro-forma EPS beats standalone EPS — an outcome of funding arithmetic. Value creation asks whether the present value of the synergies exceeds the premium paid — an NPV. Nothing forces the two to agree.

The cleanest wedge is cheap funding. Take the Tamar deal at 25 % over market: financed with 4 %-earning cash it is +20.8 % accretive *before a single synergy* — the accretion measures the gap between an 8 % earnings yield and a 3 % after-tax funding cost, and would survive a substantial overpayment intact. Double the premium and the deal still prints accretive; the extra £100m handed to Wychwood's shareholders never touches the EPS line.

So the answer to give: accretion matters because markets price off EPS, but the deal is judged by whether synergies cover the premium — and a low interest rate is not a synergy.
key_points: Accretion = EPS arithmetic; value = PV of synergies versus premium
Cheap cash or debt can make an overpriced deal comfortably accretive
Tamar all-cash: +20.8 % with zero synergies assumed
The premium overpaid never appears in the EPS calculation
Both numbers matter, for different reasons — say which answers what

follow_ups.question: Construct a deal that is accretive and destroys value.
follow_ups.answer_md: Pay £600m in cheap debt for Wychwood — a £200m premium — with no synergies at all. After-tax interest at 4.5 % on £600m is £27m; the £40m of earnings acquired still exceeds it, so EPS rises and the headline reads accretive. Meanwhile £200m has moved to the sellers with nothing coming back to cover it: NPV of roughly minus £200m, delivered with an EPS increase. The financing made the earnings maths work; nothing made the price make sense.

follow_ups.question: Can the reverse happen — a dilutive deal that creates value?
follow_ups.answer_md: Routinely. A buyer on a modest multiple paying in stock for a faster-growing business, or a pharmaceutical group buying a pre-revenue pipeline, will guide dilutive for years while acquiring assets worth more than the price. The EPS line cannot see cash flows beyond the pro-forma year, so anything whose value sits in the future — growth, a drug awaiting approval — dilutes first and pays later. Judging those deals on year-one EPS would veto some of the best ones.

weak_answer_note: "No, accretion isn't everything" without the mechanism — the cheap-funding wedge — or without being able to produce an example on request. The example is what proves the point is understood.
